articles.title: All hidden treasure locations in Onimusha Way of the Sword
articles.summary: The hidden treasures in Onimusha: Way of the Sword are a series of side quests that start once you reach the "To Live is to Suffer" main quest. When you accept one of these missions, a green circle appears on the map, indicating where you must look for the chest.
body: If the prospect of checking the streets of Eastern Kyoto for forgotten treasures while demons try to kill you doesn't sound appealing, don't fret. We've put together this guide explaining where to find all hidden treasures in Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

You can start the first Hidden Treasure side quest by talking to a woman northwest of the Gojo Street - West Spirit Mirror. The Old Drawing No. 1 shows that the treasure is on top of a building, where you can see a pagoda in the background, which is "at the top of Kiyomizu-zaka Slope."

To find this treasure, from the Kiyomizu-zaka Spirit Mirror, turn right into a narrow path that will take you behind some buildings. To your left, you will see a ladder. Use it and, once on top of the building, you will find another ladder. Climb it to reach the roof that the drawing depicts. Now, you must use your gauntlet to make the chest appear.
points: The hidden treasures in Onimusha: Way of the Sword are a series of side quests that start once you reach the "To Live is to Suffer" main quest.

articles.title: 'Ace Archer Kyoto Imperial Palace' walkthrough in Onimusha Way of the Sword
articles.summary: "Ace Archer: Kyoto Imperial Palace" is one of the secondary missions in Onimusha: Way of the Sword where you must put Musashi's bow skills into action to hunt down Kubi Akaris. Similar to the "Ace Archer: Nijo-jo Castle" story, you must find all five targets to complete this mission.
body: In this "Ace Archer: Kyoto Imperial Palace" walkthrough in Onimusha: Way of the Sword, we list the location of each Kubi Akaris below.

To unlock the "Ace Archer: Kyoto Imperial Palace" quest, you must travel to the Gojo Street - West Spirit Mirror and talk to the man to the north of it. He will tell you about flying creatures in the Kyoto Imperial Palace and ask for your help dealing with the dangerous monsters.

Your goal is to kill five Kubi Akari in the Imperial Palace zone. Although the map indicates their locations with notebook icons, you must be in the right position for your arrow to land, since the creatures are outside the explorable areas of the map. To help you, we've prepared images showing where you must position yourself (star icon) to find a specific Kubi Akari, which we've circled. We've listed the five Kubi Akari locations in the order in which we've found them, starting from the initial area of the Kyoto Imperial Castle zone, but you don't need to follow the same order.

articles.title: All swords and how to unlock them in Onimusha Way of the Sword
articles.summary: Musashi's swords are the samurai's main weapons in Onimusha: Way of the Sword to fight the legions of genma escaping from hell. Although he is capable of throwing explosive barrels at enemies and using special Oni weapons, these are circumstantial.
body: Here's how to unlock all sword skins in Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

You can unlock most swords by finding Lion Dogs. They appear after you finish the "What Lurks in the Shadows" quest and meet with Lady Murasaki. You can locate these unique dogs in fixed locations on some maps, like Eastern Kyoto. On the other hand, some swords are only available to those who pre-ordered the game or own the deluxe and premium deluxe editions.

Keep in mind that the swords you unlock in the game are merely cosmetics. Changing the skin of Musashi's swords does not change the damage they cause or add any effects to them. You can equip a sword skin by visiting any Spirit Mirror in the game and selecting the "Change Appearance" option.

articles.title: 'No One Puts Double Fine Out of Business Except for Me' — Tim Schafer Explains How He Kept Double Fine Afloat After Leaving Xbox
articles.summary: Tim Schafer, game designer and founder of Psychonauts developer Double Fine, gave a strong response after Xbox divested the studio as part of its massive restructuring efforts this summer.
body: Speaking with Bloomberg's Jason Schreier in a September 2026 interview, Schafer admitted that he knew something was up before Xbox’s divestment was officially announced — but he wasn’t about to go down without a fight.

"You’re like, 'Wait a second, we’re not going out like this,'" Schafer explained. "Some people said, 'I’m checking out, this is one too many battles for me.’ But for the rest of us, it’s like a creative awakening."

"No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me," he continued. "Asha’s not going to shoot my dog. I’m going to shoot it. But I’m not going to shoot it, because it’s going to do great. A lot of people want to walk the dog."

Thankfully, Double Fine was able to retain its intellectual property and become fully independent, though it did have to lay off a quarter of its staff as a result of this change. That isn’t stopping it from making more games, though, as the developer recently published a Kickstarter for its next project — with the addendum that if it raises $100 million, they’ll also make Brutal Legend 2.

articles.title: Wonder Woman Casting Rumors Heat Up as Fans Suspect James Gunn Secretly Picked Adria Arjona for the Role
articles.summary: DC fans are convinced the DCU's Wonder Woman will be played by Adria Arjona after she posted a video of her workout routine ahead of Man of Tomorrow.
body: As the DCU navigates its ups and downs, all eyes are on DC Studios co-CEO and director James Gunn to deliver next year's Superman sequel. Arjona is just one part of the equation that will help bring David Corenswet's Last Son of Krypton back to the big screen, but fans think she knows more than she's letting on when it comes to the part she'll play in the wider DCU.

Mixed in with a variety of other superhero parts – including Milly Alcock's Supergirl, Aaron Pierre's John Stewart, and Xolo Maridueña as Blue Beetle – Arjona was previously said to be playing the role of DC deep cut Maxima. She reportedly landed the part in April of this year, but fans think Gunn and company are misleading fans in hopes of a big Sadie Sink/Spider-Man-style surprise with Man of Tomorrow.

articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?
articles.summary: This is the first Saturday in a month I've woken up without a blocked nose or a mucus-hurling cough. Trips to Spain, Sweden, and Germany in quick succession and loaded on top of a cross country bike ride may have been a touch to much for my ageing body. Still, at last, I am well.
body: Still, at last, I am well. In body, if not in spirit. So, better start playing some games then, right?

James I'm trying to get into the Wardogs closed beta, on the grounds that - I'm told - you can ignore the gruesome gunshooty aspects of war and just spend your time ferrying crates to and from the frontlines in an old truck. Sometimes it's nice just to get away from it all.

Edwin I've managed to persuade the Gamer Network overlords to loan me a gaming laptop for reviews, so I'll be trying out various swankier 3D things on that, including Blood of Dawnwalker. I also need to finish Pathologic 3. I'm open to suggestions for recent, higher-end fare. Are they still making those Silent Hill games? What about Jak & Daxter?

Mark No games for me after two vamp-heavy weekends, I'm off to sit in a field and watch cars go round in circles near Darlington. If I'm lucky, I'll manage not to burn during the 20 minutes the sun gets out, despite being daubed in factor 50.

articles.title: gamescom Apologizes for Its Initial Response to Thefts, Promises Improved Security Measures
articles.summary: gamescom has provided a second response regarding the theft of developers’ equipment during its event, offering an apology for its initial reaction to the ordeal.
body: On August 28, 2026, indie developer Ryan Laley uploaded a video to X/Twitter claiming that all of his laptops had been stolen at gamescom. He wasn’t the only one affected; several other developers spoke out with similar stories, saying their equipment had also been pilfered at the event.
gamescom responded to the ordeal on August 29, writing that while it was "very sad" about the situation, it "would like to inform [attendees] about general security regulations."

"Individual stand security can be booked separately, and exhibitors are advised to insure equipment against theft. This is noted in the terms and conditions of participation and the technical guidelines," it said. "...At an event of this size, however, there will always be individuals attempting to take advantage of the situation. Our security measures are designed to minimize such risks as effectively as possible.”

This statement didn’t go over well. A swath of fellow exhibitors, attendees, and onlookers online felt that gamescom’s reply placed blame on victims of the theft, slamming the event for its "unacceptable response."
points: gamescom has provided a second response regarding the theft of developers’ equipment during its event, offering an apology for its initial reaction to the ordeal.

articles.summary: As we enter fall, it is once again that time of year when I find myself watching Over the Garden Wall again. It's one of those cartoons that just feels like a warm cup of cider on a chilly day. At only 10 episodes, this animated masterpiece is worthy of holding a space on your shelf.
body: Like many Cartoon Network shows, Over the Garden Wall was removed from HBO Max years ago. You can still stream it, but there's no guarantee you will be able to do so forever. Thankfully, the series got its first Blu-ray edition this year and you can buy yourself a copy. Gruv is even having a Labor Day sale right now that makes it all the more tempting to do so.

Over the Garden Wall was released on Blu-ray back in April, so it's still fairly new. Both Gruv and Amazon have it priced at almost $18 when you buy it on its own right now. So while you do have to buy two Blu-rays to actually get a discount, it's still technically cheaper to buy two copies of this Blu-ray than it is to buy one right now.

That being said, Gruv's sale includes a variety of other family favorites on Blu-ray that are definitely worth adding to your collection. First up there's The Iron Giant. This movie has won plenty of awards and will definitely make you cry if you're not careful. The signature edition includes loads of special features that are worth checking out as well.

articles.title: Game Director Finally Addresses His Rumored Foot Fetish–Wait, Not Kojima, The Other One
articles.summary: A prolific Japanese game developer has finally addressed all that weird foot imagery in his video games. What? No, I'm not talking about Hideo Kojima (he's busy hanging out with The Backrooms director right now, anyway).
body: “It's not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of--maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” Miyazaki told The Guardian in response to a question about all the hand imagery in his upcoming action-RPG, The Duskbloods. "Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from."

Though Miyazaki says he's not sure where the idea that he has a "thing for feet" comes from, it's something fans of his games have noticed for years. Whether we're talking The Maiden in Black from Demons' Souls or Priscilla (or Gwunevere, or Sister Friede, or Maneater Mildred) from Dark Souls, it's hard to ignore how many barefoot women are roaming Miyazaki's fictional worlds. Elden Ring's Malenia is rocking bare feet, too, although hers are metal prosthetics. The game's beaches even differentiate between barefoot players and those who are wearing footwear.
So what's with all the shoeless women in Souls games? According to Miyazaki, it's about depicting the human experience. Or something.
"I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe,” he elaborated.

articles.title: After AI slop accusations, Humankind 2 studio says its new trailer was definitely "made by humankind" and at least five chickens
articles.summary: A large portion of the internet pointed their virtual fingers at Humankind 2's new trailer and shouted 'AI slop!' Developer Amplitude Studios is now denying those claims and has even released a behind-the-scenes clip to prove a whole human crew (plus five chickens) made the Gamescom ONL reveal.
body: The turn-based strategy game's reveal trailer "combined live-action filmmaking, practical sets, custom-made props, costumes, visual effects, and CGI to recreate thousands of years of history in just a few seconds," the studio told Eurogamer over email. "To create the behind-the-scenes trailer, Amplitude Studios once again partnered with BETC, the creative agency behind several previous Humankind trailers."

A new behind-the-scenes video now shows that process off and, yep, those are real humans alright. "Made by humankind" sort of erases the hard work done by all those chickens, a pig, that snake, three horses and a horde of rats, though.

Humankind 2, the actual game, is promising all the historical manipulation and turn-based tinkering you would expect after the first game. This time around, the sequel's adding in an updated UI, new progression systems and improved visuals. We should hear more about what's changing soon as Humankind 2 is set to launch in 2027.
Back in 2024, the developer split from Sega during the company's widespread restructuring.

articles.title: Two Nintendo Directs Announced For Next Week, Including A Zelda Presentation
articles.summary: Not one, but two Nintendo Directs are coming next week. Nintendo has confirmed that a Legend of Zelda Direct will be held on September 8 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET, and it'll be followed by a Nintendo Direct on September 9 at the same times.
body: Rumors of a Nintendo Direct began picking up earlier this week after Ubisoft announced that a new look at Just Dance: Decades of Hits was on the way. It's worth noting that the publisher announced it for September 10, but given how often Just Dance games appear in Nintendo broadcasts, it was assumed this would be the date of a Nintendo Direct. With Nintendo hosting a September Nintendo Direct almost every year for the past decade--with 2024 being an exception--it looked like it was only a matter of time before the broadcast was officially announced.

As for what you can expect, Nintendo is keeping its lips zipped for now. Last year's September Direct was focused on several first-party games, smaller third-party titles, and the surprise reveal of a new Virtual Boy headset designed for Switch consoles, so we're guessing that it'll be more of the same for 2026. Following the release of the Switch 2 in 2025 and a steady stream of first-party games, 2026 has been slower by comparison, so here's hoping we get to see what new experiences Nintendo is working on. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is out later this month, so we'll probably get a new trailer for the turn-based tactics game.
points: Not one, but two Nintendo Directs are coming next week.

We've had a bulging bicep for No Man's Sky's Endurance update, a streaky rasher for its Beacon update, a door for Breach, and a hi-vis vest for Remnant. And that's just for starters. videos.title: Wardens of Avalon - Official Gameplay Trailer
videos.summary: Check out the Gameplay Trailer for Wardens of Avalon, a hack-and-slash action RPG developed by Runes Studio. Players will fight across a world touched by oblivion as a Twilight Knight. Craft items, upgrade gear, and claim your place at the Round Table. Wardens of Avalon is coming soon to PC (Steam).
